text:
jamal_acme: Hey, started seeing a burst of 429s on our Dedicated pool at ~10:20 PDT after we migrated to the new rate plan. Only affects /v1/generate route. Errors look like `HTTP 429` with X-Rate headers. No major CPU/GPU pressure in our metrics.

lucy_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a sample response headers + a request id? Also which dedicated pool name?

jamal_acme: pool `dedicated-eu-2-acme`, sample response: 
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1660012345
content-type: application/json

Body: {"error":"rate_limited","message":"per-tenant rate exceeded"}

We didn't change traffic pattern suddenly — single background job ramped to 10 qps for a short window.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-20261101-01 for thread 3114001234 (priority: P2).

sam_eng: Thanks — quick hypothesis: the rate plan migration may have been wired with a units-denominator mismatch (minutes vs seconds) when translating to per-tenant quota for dedicated pools. That would make 120/min inadvertently become 120/sec or vice versa. Can you confirm the plan id?

jamal_acme: Plan ID `plan_az-3-migrate`. Support portal shows 120 units but UI was vague if it's /min.

maria_sre: I'm seeing something odd on the pool side: tenant quota sampler shows "configured_rate=120" but the rate-applied metric shows 7200 tokens/min for that tenant. Looks like a multiplier=60 got applied somewhere. Also autoscaler logs show no eviction due to infra load, but the router returned 429s because per-tenant tokens were exhausted.

sam_eng: That aligns with a recent config migration script change that introduced a rate multiplier for legacy plans (to convert per-minute quotas to per-second internal units) — but the Dedicated quota writer expects per-minute values. So double conversion happened.

lucy_support: Ok can you share quick repro steps so we can validate a fix and rollback? Jamal — would you be able to run a short synthetic test? If not we can run internally against a shadow tenant.

jamal_acme: I can run a quick loop from our side. Example curl I used to reproduce: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXXX' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}' &
done
wait
```
I started getting 429s after ~100 requests.

maria_sre: Repro from our side (short version): we used a local load generator against the tenant token with 20 concurrent workers hitting /v1/generate at 1 qps each for 60s and saw X-RateLimit-Remaining hit 0 quickly even though pool GPU utilization stayed < 25%. Logs: 
```
router: tenant=acme id=rwd-req-0a1b2c3d action=throttle reason=quota_exhausted applied_quota=7200/min
quotamanager: write_quota tenant=acme configured=120 multiplier=60 effective=7200
```

sam_eng: Ok root cause confirmed: a migration script applied a multiplier when writing to the per-tenant quota store for Dedicated pools. Net result: tenants got 60x their intended allowance or the inverse depending on path, causing either silent over-throttle or accidental generosity. In this case the miswrite reduced allowed throughput (configured 120 intended/min got translated to 120/60? — our logs show effective 7200/min so we must have applied multiplier incorrectly in the rate-check path). We'll push an immediate rollback of the migration to the quota writer and patch the conversion logic.

lucy_support: Quick mitigation options for the customer: 1) temporarily bump tenant quota for acme tenant on the Dedicated pool via Console -> Dedicated -> Pool -> Tenants -> Adjust quota (we can do this if you want), 2) add a routing fallback to a compatible hosted variant (if acceptable) to avoid 429s during the rollback window. Jamal — which do you prefer?

jamal_acme: Please bump quota — we need to avoid user-facing errors for the next 30m while you roll back. Also I'll enable a short client-side retry with exponential backoff.

ops-bot: ACL request logged. Approving admins: lucy_support, sam_eng.

maria_sre: Done — bumped effective quota on `dedicated-eu-2-acme` to 7,200/min (temporary). I'm rolling the rollback PR for the migration script to revert the multiplier write. Patch: revert commit `cfg-migration#482` and update unit tests.

sam_eng: Deploying rollback to quota-writer service in staging, running sanity tests. Sanity check command we used: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer admin" https://quota.internal/pool/dedicated-eu-2-acme | jq .effective_quota` should return 120 (or desired per-minute value) after fix.

maria_sre: Rollback deployed to prod quota-writer, waiting for config refresh (TTL 30s). Monitoring tenant effective_quota metric...

maria_sre: Update — effective_quota now reads 120/min in the store and router logs show applied_quota=120/min. No new 429s in the last 60s against synthetic load.

jamal_acme: Confirmed from our side — 429s dropped and user-facing error rate back to baseline. Appreciate the quick help.

lucy_support: Thanks everyone. Action items: 
- sam_eng: add strict unit tests to migration pipeline to prevent minute<->second conversions from double-applying.
- maria_sre: add an alert on "applied_quota / configured_quota > 10" anomaly for Dedicated pools.
- ops-bot: postmortem ticket INC-20261101-01-POST with RCA and timeline.

sam_eng: I'll follow up with a short PR and add a regression test.

jamal_acme: tagging here once postmortem is available, thanks. :thumbsup:
